article_blocks: Why go
Korea's capital and the country's main international gateway — most first-time visitors start here, and it's the easiest base for day trips.
When to go
Spring (Apr) and autumn (Oct–Nov) have the mildest, driest weather. Summer (Jul–Aug) is hot and humid with a monsoon season; winter (Dec–Feb) is cold and dry.
Getting there
Incheon Airport (ICN) or Gimpo (GMP). From ICN, the AREX express train reaches Seoul Station in about 45 minutes.
Do this
Walk Bukchon Hanok Village early, before the tour groups arrive
Eat your way through Gwangjang Market's street-food stalls
Ride the cable car or hike up to N Seoul Tower for a skyline view
Where to stay
Budget: A guesthouse near Dongdaemun or Sinchon — close to subway lines, easy for a first trip
Mid: A mid-range hotel in Myeongdong or Jongno — walkable to major sights
Splurge: A hotel in Gangnam or near Han River — for river or skyline views

article_blocks: The vibe
Seoul's shopping district: department stores, beauty shops and street food, with a 1898 brick cathedral in the middle. Very international, very busy.

posts.hook: The JR Pass: still worth it?
bullets: Japan Rail raised the price in Oct 2023, so it now mostly pays off for long point-to-point trips (e.g. Tokyo–Osaka–Hiros
article_blocks: What it covers
Unlimited rides on JR trains nationwide (excluding the fastest Nozomi/Mizuho Shinkansen), for 7/14/21 days.
Worth it?

Japan Rail raised the price in Oct 2023, so it now mostly pays off for long point-to-point trips (e.g. Tokyo–Osaka–Hiroshima round trip). For a single-region trip, a regional JR pass or individual tickets are usually cheaper — check the fare calculator before buying.

Seoul (Yeouido, Jinhae) and Tokyo (Meguro River, Ueno) both peak around the same week most years, but forecasts shift year to year — check the official forecast about 2–3 weeks out before booking around it.
